title: How to Trade With a 9-5 Job (TTrades Fractal Model Explained)
description: Learn how to trade with a 9 to 5 job using weekly bias, daily swing points, hourly entries, and the TTrades Fractal Model.

body.text: Introduction
If you work a full time job, spending hours watching charts is not always realistic.

Many traders think they need to scalp or trade lower timeframes to fit trading into their schedule. I lean the other way. The higher timeframes can give you a way to spend less time on the charts while still finding quality setups.
The idea is simple.
Start with a weekly bias. Align daily swing points with that direction. Then use the daily and hourly Fractal Model to find entries.
Instead of constantly watching price, focus on candle closures and check the charts at specific times.
Start With a Weekly Bias
The first thing to establish is the weekly bias.
Ask yourself one question: Is price reaching for the previous week’s high or low?
You can also use weekly candle closures to establish direction. A Candle 2 or Candle 3 closure can give you an idea of where price may expand next.

For example, if the weekly candle closes bullish, you can anticipate further expansion higher. That does not mean price has to move in that direction immediately. You still need to see how the daily structure develops.
The weekly timeframe gives you the overall direction to work with.
Align Daily Swing Points With The Weekly Bias
Once you have a weekly bias, look for daily swing points that align with it.
If the weekly direction is bullish, look for daily lows that can lead to expansion higher.
If the weekly direction is bearish, look for daily highs that can lead to expansion lower.
The phases of price are useful here.
Price can expand, retrace, and form a new swing point before continuing. Rather than trying to trade every move, look for a daily swing that gives you a way to get on side with the weekly direction.
You do not need a setup every day. You need a clear daily structure that aligns with your higher timeframe idea.
Use The Daily And Hourly Fractal Model
Once you have the weekly bias and a daily swing point, use the daily and hourly Fractal Model to find entries.
The logic is based on candle closures.
A new hourly candle forms every hour. If you are working an eight hour shift, you can check the chart around the top of each hour instead of watching it continuously.
That could mean eight minutes of chart time across an entire workday.
The goal is to let the daily wick form and then look for an entry as price trades away from it.
You can use swing point entries, candle closure entries, or positional entries. The preferred approach is an intra candle change in the state of delivery when the setup provides it.
Once the entry forms, use the protected swing or relevant structure for invalidation and define your target.
Let The Daily Wick Form
The daily wick is an important part of this approach.
If you have a bullish daily idea, you want to see price form a low and then trade higher. If you have a bearish daily idea, you want to see price form a high and then trade lower.
A protected swing can help identify when that wick may have formed.
For example, if price forms a protected swing near the daily open and the structure aligns with your direction, you can look to enter with your stop beyond that swing.
You are not trying to predict the exact daily high or low. You are waiting for structure to form that gives you a defined entry and invalidation.
Focus On The Sessions That Fit Your Schedule
You do not need to trade every session.
If you are in a US time zone, you can focus on the Asia session to see whether you can position for the day. If that setup does not form, you can check again during New York.
The same model can be applied across different sessions. The important part is having a routine that fits your schedule.
Check the chart at planned times. Look for the setup. If there is no valid entry, move on.
You Can Still Use Positional Entries
Waiting for an intra candle change in the state of delivery gives you additional confirmation, but it can also mean missing a move.
Sometimes price will not form the continuation you are waiting for.
That does not mean the model has failed. It means the specific entry you were waiting for did not appear.
A positional entry is another way to approach the setup when the context supports it.

For example, you may expect EQ to hold and look for 50% of the change in the state of delivery to hold as well. Your stop would need to sit beyond the relevant structure, often around the body of the opposing candle.
This can give you a way to enter without waiting for additional confirmation. However, it also means accepting a different entry condition and its risk.
Choose the entry method that fits your rules. You will not catch every move, and that is fine.
Use Continuations To Stay With The Move
The first entry is not the only opportunity.
Once price reverses and begins expanding in your direction, further continuations can form along the way.
In a bearish model, look for lower highs. In a bullish model, look for higher lows.
These continuation entries can help you get on side even if the initial swing point entry was missed.
The overall idea remains the same. Establish the higher timeframe context, wait for structure, and use the Fractal Model to find an entry.
When The Setup Fails
Not every entry will work.
A protected swing can form and then fail. If you take the entry according to your rules and price reaches your invalidation, that is a valid loss.
The important part is to avoid forcing another entry simply because the first one failed.
Wait for new structure. If another valid continuation forms, evaluate it on its own.
The model is built around candle closures, structure, and defined invalidation. Your job is to follow those conditions rather than trying to make every setup work.
Hold For The Larger Range
One benefit of aligning the daily setup with the weekly direction is that you may have room to hold beyond the initial target.
A daily setup can sometimes provide 2R within the same daily range. If the weekly direction remains intact, there may also be an opportunity to hold for further expansion toward the weekly target.
Your target depends on the structure and the amount of range available.
You can take your planned profit or hold a portion of the position for a larger move, provided the trade still follows your rules.
The key is to know what you are targeting before entering.
The Mechanical Process
Start by establishing the weekly direction using the previous week’s high or low, or a weekly candle closure. Then find daily swing points that align with that direction.
Use the daily and hourly Fractal Model to confirm structure and identify an entry. Let the daily wick form, wait for a valid entry condition, and define your invalidation and target before entering.
Check the charts around candle closures rather than watching price all day. If the move develops, look for continuation opportunities as long as the structure remains valid.
Final Thoughts
If you work a full time job, you do not need to spend more time on the charts. You need a process that makes your chart time more focused.
Start with the weekly direction. Find daily swing points that align with it. Then use the daily and hourly Fractal Model to find your entries.
Check the charts around candle closures. Wait for the structure to form. Take the setup when your rules are met.
The goal is to spend less time watching price and more time executing a clear model.
Keep it mechanical.
